name: Thymosin Fraction 5
lead: Thymosin fraction 5 (TF5) is a partially purified extract of calf thymus prepared in 1972 by Allan Goldstein's group, which contains many small peptides, including the later-characterized thymosin alpha-1 and thymosin beta-4 [1][2][3][4]. It was the starting material from which individual thymosins were purified, and it was tested in patients before the purified peptides existed.

Its relevance to looksmaxxing is as a root of the thymic peptide family. Thymosin beta-4 and thymosin alpha-1 are the forms that appear in recovery, longevity and research-peptide discussions, where people hope for faster tissue repair and better immune resilience, which supports training and general appearance over time. Published clinical work focuses on purified thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin) in infection and cancer, not on TF5 for appearance [5][6].
The extract itself is no longer a typical consumer product, and no approved use of crude TF5 was found.

paras: Work on thymic extracts began in the 1960s with Abraham White and then Allan Goldstein, who showed that extracts restored immune function in animals lacking a thymus [2][7]. Goldstein, a biochemist who later chaired biochemistry at George Washington University from 1978 to 2009, co-discovered the thymosins with White [14]. TF5 was reported to contain over 40 peptides of roughly 1,000 to 15,000 daltons, grouped as alpha, beta and gamma thymosins; they are structurally unrelated, and some are widespread in tissues rather than thymus-specific [7].

A 2018 paper in Expert Opinion on Biological Therapy re-evaluated TF5 after 35 years using high-resolution mass spectrometry, revisiting what the original fraction really contains [15]. Later reviews describe beta-thymosins as a family of actin-binding proteins with intracellular and extracellular activities [16][17].

Thymosin alpha-1 was isolated and sequenced in 1977 and 1979 [3][8][9], and bovine thymosin beta-4 was sequenced in 1981 [4]. Later work found that alpha-1 derives from a larger precursor, prothymosin alpha [10].

Thymosin alpha-1 was isolated and sequenced in 1977 and 1979 [3][8][9], and bovine thymosin beta-4 was sequenced in 1981 [4]. Later work found that alpha-1 derives from a larger precursor, prothymosin alpha [10]. Wikipedia's biography of Goldstein reports that thymosin alpha-1 was the first thymosin to enter clinical trials and is approved in China and more than 30 other countries, and that thymosin beta-4 has been studied for wound healing in ulcers and dry eye, with an injectable form under development by RegeneRx Biopharmaceuticals, where Goldstein is chief scientific advisor [14].

Thymic hormones were studied as a link between immune aging and endocrine function. A 1999 review of the thymus-pituitary axis reviews reports that TF5, thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 affected beta-endorphin, ACTH, glucocorticoid, LHRH and LH secretion in animal and cell models, and that aging changes pituitary responsiveness to thymic hormones [18]. A 1981 Science paper reported that thymosin stimulated luteinizing hormone-releasing factor secretion [19]. Reviews in the 1980s examined thymosins and the immunology of aging [20]. These strands underlie the longevity interest, but they are laboratory and review-level observations.

sections.h: Research use in cancer and transplantation
paras: A Cochrane review of randomized trials of purified thymus extracts and synthetic thymic peptides alongside chemotherapy or radiotherapy in adults with cancer identified 26 trials with 2,736 patients; 20 tested extracts (thymostimulin or thymosin fraction 5) and six tested synthetic peptides (thymopentin or thymosin alpha-1) [21]. A 1983 study reported that TF5 did not accelerate reconstitution of immune reactivity after human marrow grafting [22], and a 1988 report followed patients who received thymic grafts or factors after marrow transplantation for 2 to 12 years [23].

TF5 itself is not a typical consumer product; purified peptides derived from it, chiefly thymosin alpha-1 and thymosin beta-4, are what appear in research-peptide markets and in recovery and longevity discussions. Thymosin alpha-1 is an approved drug in China and other countries under the name thymalfasin, according to Goldstein's biography [14]. No approved use of the extract was found.

No studies of crude TF5 as an appearance intervention were found. Clinical research on thymic preparations includes the Cochrane meta-analysis of 26 cancer trials, of which most tested extracts such as TF5 or thymostimulin [21]; a placebo-controlled pilot trial of thymosin in chronic hepatitis B in 1991 [11] and a review of thymalfasin for that disease [24]; and a clinical-trial review of thymic hormones in patients with phobic disorders [25]. Registered phase 2 trials test thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin) in cancer settings, including pneumonia prevention in lung cancer (n=69), advanced refractory solid tumors and metastatic esophageal cancer [5][6][12]. Laboratory work also reported effects of thymic hormones on natural killer cell activity [13].

card.summary: The calf-thymus extract that thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were purified from; relevant here only as their source.
card.note: Mixture; no approved use or appearance data.

quick.overview:
Thymosin fraction 5 is a calf-thymus extract made in 1972 that contains dozens of peptides. Thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were later purified from it.

It has no appearance evidence; clinical studies concern purified thymosin alpha-1 in infection and cancer.
quick.mechanism: The extract restored immune function in thymus-deficient animals, which led to the idea of thymic hormones; individual peptides have different actions.
quick.risks: No approved use of the extract was found, and no appearance-related safety data. Animal-derived mixtures vary in composition.

chain: Thymus-derived peptides signal to immune and other cells
Immune support and, for thymosin beta-4, wound-repair biology
Proposed healthier ageing and faster tissue recovery (claimed)
angle.text: Thymosin fraction 5 is the historical starting material for the thymic peptides sold today as research chemicals. People who follow thymic peptides hope for immune resilience, recovery and slower ageing, but the extract's own clinical record is in immune and cancer settings, not appearance.
